# Atmospherics Tools Atmospheric technicians have the same basic set of tools as engineers, but they also have access to two special tools: the holofan projector and gas analyzer.
## Holofan projector The holofan projector is a tool that creates a barrier of solid light. It blocks the flow of air and gases while allowing people to pass through it.
This is very useful for moving through [textlink="firelock buffers" link="FireAndGasControl"] without allowing gas to leak between rooms, as well as for warning the crew that entering a room may be dangerous. It can also be used as a temporary barrier that lets crew members move quickly between depressurized and pressurized areas without risking the loss of air from adjacent rooms.
It has an internal charge that is consumed with each use. To recharge it, remove the battery and place it in a battery charger or recharger.
Holofans placed next to a [textlink="firelock" link="FireAndGasControl"] disable its interlock, allowing it to be opened manually.
## Gas analyzer The gas analyzer is a tool used to examine the gas composition of the surrounding atmosphere or any [textlink="atmospheric device" link="GasManipulation"] containing gas.
To use the gas analyzer, click on a [textlink="device" link="GasManipulation"] containing gas or on the air in a room.
When used, the gas analyzer reports: - The volume of the device being measured, not the volume of the gas - The total gas pressure in kPa - The gas temperature in kelvin (K) and degrees Celsius (C) - The exact gas composition in moles and as a percentage of the total volume
At the bottom of its interface, the gas analyzer displays a visual representation of the different [textlink="gases" link="Gasses"] in the mixture and their relative concentrations.
When analyzing binary and ternary [textlink="devices" link="GasManipulation"], meaning devices with two or three inputs or outputs, the gas analyzer displays the composition of each input and output separately. This is useful for diagnosing problems in gas [textlink="mixing and filtering" link="MixingAndFiltering"] setups.
